balloons.text: They are improving.
You sound almost pleased.
Almost.
If you insist on naming bastions after me, I insist on at least choosing a decent symbol.
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: Better a tooth than a sore. At least this one bites outward.
The Deccan rider and the Dutch captain.
Two foreigners teaching us how to use our own land.
Teaching us how to keep it.
If you prefer to learn from men who have never seen a European musket up close, that is your choice. Do not complain when your sons bleed for it.
We must not become a separate standard. If they see us as a force within a force, we will be cut out like a tumour when the monarchy changes.
You think that will happen?
In my land, kings fall. In yours, too.
We fight for the structure, then. Not the man.
We fight so that whoever sits on that platform cannot easily undo what we have built. It is a selfish defence, in a way.
Selfish defence keeps people alive.
Stone where you must. Earth where you can.
You spend as much time keeping us from killing each other as keeping the king alive.
It is all the same work. Preventable deaths exhaust me.
Again.
Breathe. The gun does not fear your heartbeat.
Make it go slower than the drum.
Good.
Now do it when someone is shouting in your ear.
Yes, Kappittan. Yes, Pillai.
The Dutch are no longer the only storm. There are new flags at the northern ports.
We will need more than one tooth. And more than one kind of jaw.
You and De Lannoy are useful.
You are also convenient scapegoats.
Scapegoats?
If the army fails, they will say the foreigner misled it. If it grows too strong, they will say the foreigner twisted it.
If a wall ever falls, I would rather it land on the Dutchman who designed it than on my people.
You make the future sound bleak.
I make it sound like what it often is.
Complicated.
This is what my army will wear.
The drill is European. The muskets are European. The forts are built to European designs.
It is time the men who use these things look as if they belong to the same army.
Maharaja, our men have always worn...
What they pleased.
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: When a Dutch officer looks through his glass at my lines, I want him to see something that makes his stomach turn.
Not a rabble. A machine.
You have seen European armies. Tell them.
In Europe, when regiments dress alike, they move alike.
When an enemy sees a line of men dressed the same, he sees not individuals but a wall. Walls are harder to break than crowds.
And when those walls wear coats like his own army's, the enemy hesitates. He wonders if his maps are wrong.
Hesitation kills.
You have concerns, Pillai.
I have served you in my own clothes. They have not prevented me from drilling your horse.
No. But your horse are a small part of this army. When the full force marches, I want one face. Not many.
The men will resist. They will see this as...
Foreign. Yes. As they saw muskets once. As they saw star forts.
They learned. So will you.
Coats will be issued within the month. Officers will set the example.
Dismissed.
You are thinking of Goa.
I am thinking of many things.
You are thinking that this coat looks like the coat of the men who broke your fingers and chained you in a ship's hold.
It is not the same coat. The men who wear it will not be the same men.
Knowing and feeling are different animals.
Yes. They are. But I do not have time to wait for your feelings to catch up with your knowledge.
Other Europeans will come. When they do, I want them to see an army that they recognise and fear.
Talk to De Lannoy. He wears the coat already.
Ask him how it sits on a man who once wore a different one.
You stayed behind. I assume you did not simply want to admire the buttons.
The king told me to speak with you. About wearing the coat.
Ah.
When the fort burned at Colachel, I expected to die.
What I did not expect was to be offered a choice.
Serve Travancore, or rot in a cell until the company forgot my name.
They would not have lifted a finger. I knew too much about their failures.
Dead men cannot testify.
The first time I put on Travancore colours, I felt as if I had swallowed broken glass.
My mother would light candles for a son who had become, in their eyes, a traitor.
And now?
Now it is cloth. It keeps the sun off my shoulders and the rain off my back.
The man inside has not changed. He has simply learned to wear a different skin.
You chose this. You accepted the king's offer.
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: I did not choose to look like a Portuguese guard.
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: No. But you chose to stay. To drill these men. To build these walls with me.
Each of those choices was a thread. The coat is simply the weaving.
In Goa, there was an officer.
He was very particular about his cuffs.
He would come each morning, and check his cuffs before he gave orders.
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: The coat was always clean. Even when there was blood on the floor.
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: He would step around it, so as not to stain his shoes.
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: Then he would leave, and the guards would do what he had ordered.
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: And the coat would walk out as spotless as it had walked in.
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: And when you see this coat...
I see his cuffs. I see his shoes. I see the door closing behind him while I hung from the chains and wondered how many more mornings I could survive.
I cannot make that memory disappear. No one can.
But I can tell you what I have learned about clothes and men.
In Zeeland, where I was born, there is a saying: the shirt does not make the sailor, but it tells you which ship he serves.
I simply chose a different ship.
And if the ship is wrong?
Then you are wrong with it. But you are wrong *together*.
That is what the coat means. When you stand in a line with these men, you are telling the world: we fight as one.
The Portuguese who tortured you were not evil because of their coats.
They were evil because of what they chose to do while wearing them.
You have the same choice.
You can wear this cloth and be the man who trains cavalry to protect Padmini's fields.
Or you can refuse, and be the man who could not see past his scars to what his king was building.
You make it sound simple.
It is not simple.
Some mornings I look at the coat on its peg and feel that glass in my throat again.
Then I put it on. And I go to the wall. And I do the work.
Eventually, the glass becomes smaller.
I will wear it.
The first few days will be difficult. You will want to tear it off and burn it.
I recommend against burning it. The quartermaster is very particular about inventory.
I will try to restrain myself.
The same drills. Different cloth.
Mount up.
The Viceroy sends his compliments. And his curiosity. Pepper, as always.
The Dutch came for pepper too. We know how that ended.
The king wants them to see our officers.
Senhor... I... that is...
Father Duarte. You have come a long way from Goa.
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: You survived. The ship... we heard it was lost in a storm.
Most of it was.
I did not.
I have thought of you. Over the years. I have wondered...
Whether I would come for you?
Whether you found what you were fighting for.
That night, in the chamber, you said God favours whoever has the better powder.
It seems you found the better powder.
I found something. Whether it is what I was fighting for, I am still deciding.
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: I could have you arrested.
Some of these men lost brothers in your dungeons. Some of them lost more.
You could. It would not be unjust.
No. It would not.
But I am not going to.
Do you know why?
Because you hesitated.
In the chamber, when João reached for the brazier, you stopped him.
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: At the gate, you made the sign of the cross. Not the quick one, the one that wards off evil.
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: The slow one. The one that asks for something.
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: I asked for your forgiveness.
I have asked for it every day since.
I cannot give you that. What was done to me is not mine alone to forgive.
Keshavrao drowned in that storm. Others died in your cells. Their forgiveness is not mine to grant.
I wear this coat now. I drill these men.
The man you tortured is gone.
The man who stands here now has made his choices. Some of them haunt me. Some of them I am proud of. Most are somewhere in between.
Then we are alike in that. More than I would have thought.
Perhaps.
When you return to Goa, tell them what you saw here.
Tell them that the man they branded as property now commands the cavalry that guards this coast.
My uncle says I am to learn from you.
Learn what?
How to stay alive when men want me dead.
Your uncle could have sent you to De Lannoy.
De Lannoy teaches formations. My uncle says you teach survival.
They stay at the gate. On the training ground, you are not a prince. You are a student.
If I strike you, they do not interfere. If you fall, they do not help you rise.
Highness, the Maharaja's orders were...
To learn from this man. I cannot learn if I am wrapped in silk. Go.
What first?
First, you learn how much you do not know.
You are trying to kill the heir.
I am trying to make him harder to kill. There is a difference.
The Senior Rani has concerns.
Continue. A king who is distracted by his mother will be distracted by everything.
Highness. You could have summoned me to the palace.
I wished to see. There is a difference between reports and observation.
He has changed. The way he stands. Even the servants have noticed. And the cost?
Bruises. A few cuts that will scar. Nothing that will not heal.
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: When he was born, my brother held him and wept.
I have spent fourteen years keeping him alive. Tasters, guards, astrologers.
Now I send him to you because all my counting has made him soft.
At the temple, he stood like a deer in torchlight.
He will not freeze again. I am burning that out of him.
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: I know. That is why I have not stopped you.
A mother's fear can become a son's chains.
This was my grandmother's. It passes from woman to woman in this house.
Then why give it to me?
I am not giving it to you. I am showing it to you.
So that you understand what you are training. Not a soldier. Not a prince. A line.
If you break him, I will have you killed. Slowly. With full knowledge of what is happening to you.
I understand, Highness.
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: He says you tell him unpleasant truths. Continue.
She likes you.
She threatened to have me killed slowly.
Yes. That is how you know. The ones she does not like, she simply has killed. Without warning.
In the Deccan, a man's horse is his second self.
Our kings ride elephants.
Elephants are for show. A horse can take you where elephants cannot. Away from danger, when danger is the only certainty.
Pillai. At the temple, when the chaver came, I froze.
I saw the blade and I could not move. If my uncle had not...
He did. That is what matters.
You were ten years old. A boy can be forgiven.
I am not ten now.
If it happens again, your body will know what to do before your mind has time to be afraid.
And if instinct is not enough?
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: Then you die. But you die moving, not standing still.
You do not speak to me like the others do.
The others speak around the truth. You speak through it.
The heir cannot be treated like a common soldier.
That is the point.
The men look at me differently now.
They look at you as one of them. Is that not what you wanted?
I do not know what I wanted.
I only knew I did not want to be the boy at the temple again. The one who stood there while others bled for him.
You will never be that boy again. You have made certain of it.
Thank you, Pillai. For not treating me like glass.
Glass breaks. You are iron that has not yet been forged. The fire is uncomfortable. But it is necessary.
Then I will try to enjoy the burning.
My grandfather cast cannon for the Zamorin. My father cast them for Kochi. I cast them for Travancore.
The metal does not care which king pays for the mould.
You do not pray to the same gods as your men.
No. But we bleed the same colour. That is enough for a gun crew.
The Dutch and the Portuguese think history began when their ships arrived.
This coast has buried empires before them. It will bury more.
And yet we wear their coats now. And fire their cannons.
We wear what is useful. We fire what works.
That is not surrender. That is wisdom.
Avraham ben Ephraim. His family has traded with mine for four generations.
The man who teaches horses to dance with muskets.
The man who tries.
The Jews of Kochi have a saying.
The Portuguese came and went, the Dutch came and are going, the English are coming. We remain.
I doubt all kings. But this king pays his debts. That is worth something.
We have outlasted Pharaohs and Caesars and Inquisitors. We will outlast kings of pepper, too.
Strange allies, these.
All allies are strange. Until you need them.
Your swords are better for cutting from horseback. Our straight blades are better for thrusts on foot.
We make do with what the land asks. If the ground is cluttered, curve your steel.
If we are to be blamed together, we may as well be armed together.
balloons.tail: tail to the panel edge (off-panel speaker)

balloons.text: You have accepted that you will never go back.
Back where? To ships that would call me traitor? To a land that has already written my name in a different set of books?
This is my fort now. These are my men.
If I spend the rest of my life making sure they do not die as stupidly as some of my countrymen did, perhaps that will be enough to balance a few lines.
Under whose standard do we truly stand, Ananthan Pillai?
The king's? The idea of this place? The memory of the men who died at Colachel?
All of them. On different days.
On the days when it is the king's, we must be careful. Kings change. Places endure longer.
You have been talking to Revathi.
She scolds me too. Apparently my foreignness does not exempt me.
